name: US Health News
tagline: Outbreaks, recalls and public health, explained.

articles.title: Metoclopramide Tablets Recalled Over Cross-Contamination With Other Medications
articles.description: The FDA has issued a Class II recall for Safecor Health's metoclopramide tablets 5 mg, lot 3116509, after cross-contamination with other medications was found, according to the FDA enforcement report of November 4, 2026.
articles.sources: FDA Enforcement Report, November 4, 2026, via HMP Global Learning Network, November 5, 2026
articles.body:
The US Food and Drug Administration has issued a voluntary Class II recall for metoclopramide tablets, USP, 5 mg, after cross-contamination with other medications was identified, according to the FDA enforcement report published on November 4, 2026.

The affected batch is lot 3116509, which expires in July 2027. The recall was initiated by Safecor Health, LLC, based in Rockford, Illinois, on October 6, 2026, and received its Class II classification on October 23, 2026. A Class II recall covers a quality issue that is likely to cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences, or carries a low probability of serious adverse health consequences.

What metoclopramide is used for

Metoclopramide is used to treat gastroparesis — a condition in which the stomach empties too slowly — and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). Patients who take the medicine should check the lot number on their packaging and, if it matches lot 3116509, contact their dispensing pharmacist or prescribing clinician for guidance on a replacement supply.

What patients should do

Patients should not stop a prescribed medicine abruptly without speaking to a clinician or pharmacist, since sudden discontinuation carries its own risks. The recall is limited to the single identified lot, and the reports checked did not name any other lots or strengths as affected. Anyone who has taken tablets from the recalled lot and has concerns about symptoms should seek medical advice promptly, and pharmacists can arrange a replacement from an unaffected batch.

articles.title: FDA Warns Parents Not to Serve Once Upon a Farm Toddler Bars After Choking Reports
articles.description: The FDA has advised consumers not to buy or serve Once Upon a Farm Tractor Wheels Organic Toddler Soft-Baked Bars after reports of toddlers suffering complete airway obstruction, in a safety communication dated October 30, 2026.
articles.body:
The US Food and Drug Administration has advised consumers not to buy or serve Once Upon a Farm Tractor Wheels Organic Toddler Soft-Baked Bars, after receiving several reports of toddlers suffering complete airway obstruction after eating the product, according to an FDA safety communication dated October 30, 2026.

The reports describe toddlers aged about 1.5 to 2.5 years who were unable to breathe after consuming the bars. The FDA said consumers should not buy or serve the product and should immediately throw it away. The agency said it would update its advisory as more information becomes available.

Where the bars are sold

The product is sold nationwide, online and in stores including Costco, Target and Walmart, according to the FDA advisory. Parents and caregivers who have the bars at home should check their pantry and discard them rather than passing them on to another household.

What to do if a child has eaten one

Complete airway obstruction is a medical emergency: a child who cannot breathe, cough or cry needs immediate emergency help. Parents who are concerned about a child who ate one of the bars should seek medical attention promptly, even if the child appears to have recovered, and should report the incident to the FDA so the agency can track the scale of the problem. The advisory is a warning about this specific product, not about other toddler foods, and the FDA has not reported a recall of other Once Upon a Farm products in this communication.

articles.title: CVS Health to Split Into Two Companies: Pharmacies in One, Aetna and Caremark in the Other
articles.description: CVS Health confirmed on November 4 it will split into two publicly traded companies — CVS Pharmacy with about 9,000 stores, and a healthcare company holding Aetna and Caremark — with completion targeted for the first half of 2028.
articles.sources: CVS Health announcement via CNN, Becker's Payer, Fierce Healthcare, November 4, 2026
articles.body:
CVS Health confirmed on Wednesday, November 4, that it will split into two independent, publicly traded companies, marking one of the largest shakeups in the US healthcare industry and unwinding the vertically integrated model built over nearly two decades, reports said.

The two companies

One company, to be called CVS Pharmacy, will hold approximately 9,000 retail pharmacies, the mail-order pharmacy business, MinuteClinic including virtual care, and the Health100 technology services business, led by current group president Prem Shah as chief executive. The other, referred to as CVS Health in the interim, will hold insurer Aetna, pharmacy benefit manager CVS Caremark, CVS Specialty, Oak Street Health and Signify Health, led by current chairman and chief executive David Joyner. Shareholders will own shares in both companies in a transaction intended to be tax-free.

Timing, earnings — and what does not change yet

The separation is targeted for completion in the first half of 2028, and until then CVS will continue to operate as it does today, the company said. CVS also reported third-quarter results on November 4: net profit of nearly $2.2 billion, up from a $4 billion net loss a year earlier, and revenue of $108.4 billion, up 5.4 percent. The company said the split would have little impact on how people shop at CVS and would not change what they pay for prescriptions; shares fell about 10 percent in early trading after initially ticking up premarket, CNN reported.

articles.title: FDA Tentatively Approves First Generic Lenacapavir, Priced at $40 a Year in 120 Countries
articles.description: The FDA has tentatively approved Dr. Reddy's generic version of injectable lenacapavir, the first generic long-acting HIV prevention shot cleared by the agency, priced at $40 per person per year in 120 low- and middle-income countries.
articles.body:
The US Food and Drug Administration has granted tentative approval to Dr. Reddy's Laboratories for a generic version of injectable lenacapavir, the first generic long-acting HIV prevention injection cleared by the agency, reports said on November 4.

What tentative approval means

Tentative approval confirms the product meets FDA standards for safety, efficacy and manufacturing, but keeps it off the US market while Gilead's patents run; it allows US government programmes to buy it for use abroad. Dr. Reddy's generic is priced at $40 per person per year in 120 low- and middle-income countries, and first supplies should reach countries before the end of 2026, with wider availability in 2027, reports said.

The context

The clearance comes 16 months after Gilead's original lenacapavir won FDA approval in June 2025. Dr. Reddy's filed the prevention and treatment uses together under the FDA's 505(b)(2) pathway, which qualified the application for priority review with a six-month target. Lenacapavir is a twice-yearly injection; the generic approval is a regulatory milestone for HIV prevention access, not a change to US availability, which remains patent-blocked for now.

articles.title: FDA Recalls Thousands of Blood Pressure Medicine Bottles Over Excess Levels and Failed Tests
articles.description: The FDA announced recalls of two blood pressure combination medicines — 21,620 bottles of Viatris telmisartan/amlodipine and 3,744 bottles of Macleods olmesartan combination tablets — over excess drug levels and failed dissolution tests.
articles.sources: Health and Me, Dispatch Times, November 3, 2026
articles.body:
The US Food and Drug Administration has announced nationwide recalls of two blood pressure medications over concerns about excess drug levels and manufacturing quality failures, reports on November 3 said.

What was recalled

The FDA announced a Class III recall of Viatris Inc.'s combination telmisartan and amlodipine tablets (40 mg/5 mg) because they may contain more telmisartan than specified — 21,620 bottles in total, in 30-count bottles across lots 3228113, 3228114 and 3228115 (expiry October 31) and lots 3228120 and 3228121 (expiry November 30). Class III means use of the affected product is not likely to cause adverse health consequences, and the FDA did not specify how much additional telmisartan the tablets may contain.

The second recall

The FDA also recalled 3,744 bottles of a Macleods Pharmaceuticals combination of olmesartan medoxomil, amlodipine and hydrochlorothiazide (40 mg/10 mg/12.5 mg) after the tablets failed dissolution specifications — the test of whether a medicine dissolves at the required rate. The company began the recall on October 7, and the FDA classified it as Class II on October 26, meaning use could cause temporary or medically reversible health problems, though serious harm is considered unlikely. Patients should not stop a prescribed blood pressure medicine without speaking to their clinician or pharmacist, and should check lot numbers against the recall notice.

articles.title: Energy Drinks and Cardiac Arrest: What a New Study Actually Shows — and What It Doesn't
articles.description: A study presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026 found cardiac arrest appeared about 11 times more often in FDA reports involving stimulant products — but researchers stress it shows association, not proof of cause.
articles.body:
A new study has renewed scrutiny of energy drinks and stimulant-containing supplements, finding cardiac arrest appeared about 11 times more often in US Food and Drug Administration adverse-event reports involving caffeine and stimulant-containing products than in reports involving products without those ingredients, Times Now reported on November 3.

What the researchers found

Presented as research to be discussed at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026, the analysis examined 28,345 adverse-event reports submitted to an FDA safety database between 2017 and 2025. Of these, 854 involved energy drinks or dietary supplements containing caffeine and other stimulants, while 27,491 concerned products without those ingredients. Reports involving stimulant-containing products were also about 4.5 times more likely to mention heart attacks, and reports of ventricular arrhythmias and heart palpitations were around four times more common. Adults aged 18 to 34 accounted for around 45 percent of the reports linking these products to cardiovascular events.

The crucial caveat

Researchers stressed the findings establish an association, not a direct cause-and-effect relationship. The analysis relied on voluntarily submitted FDA reports, so it cannot establish how frequently cardiac events occur among all energy drink consumers or prove that the products triggered them, and the research is preliminary and has not yet undergone peer review as a full scientific paper. Readers should not treat social-media summaries as medical advice; anyone with concerns about caffeine, stimulants and heart risk should consult a clinician.

articles.title: FDA to Review uniQure's Huntington's Gene Therapy, Decision Due by May 2027
articles.description: The FDA has accepted uniQure's application for its Huntington's disease gene therapy AMT-130 and will decide by May 1, 2027, ending a standoff in which an agency official had called the treatment a 'failed product.'
articles.body:
Dutch gene therapy developer uniQure said on Monday that the US Food and Drug Administration had accepted its application for its Huntington's disease treatment and would decide on the drug by May 1, 2027, Reuters reported on November 2. US-listed shares of the company were up 2.5 percent in premarket trading.

An accelerated review after a reversal

The FDA granted the therapy a faster review under its accelerated approval pathway, which can allow speedier approval for serious diseases based on early evidence while requiring the company to confirm the benefit in future studies. The agency is also considering holding a meeting of outside experts to discuss the application. The decision ends a lengthy standoff during which a senior agency official described the treatment as a 'failed product'; the regulator later reversed course and agreed to review it.

What the application rests on

UniQure's application is based on early- to mid-stage study results comparing treated patients with a group from an external Huntington's disease database. The company said it has treated 51 patients across its studies so far, after AMT-130 failed to slow disease progression in a four-year trial — the result that sent its shares sharply lower months ago. UniQure plans to begin US patient screening by year-end for a 200-patient follow-up trial, with two-thirds receiving the gene therapy and the rest standard care. Acceptance for review is not an approval.

articles.title: 'Dark Nutrition' Fans Drink Raw Milk, but FDA and CDC Flag the Catch
articles.description: Raw milk and uncooked organ meats are in the spotlight after a New York Times Magazine investigation into 'dark nutrition' — but the FDA says pasteurization costs nothing nutritionally, and the CDC warns farm practices cannot guarantee safety.
articles.body:
Raw milk's appeal does not erase the infection risk of skipping pasteurization, Men's Journal reported on November 1, summarizing an October 21 New York Times Magazine investigation into so-called 'dark nutrition' — overlapping communities questioning conventional food advice, rather than one standardized eating plan.

What the agencies say

The FDA says research shows 'no meaningful difference between the nutrient content of pasteurized and unpasteurized milk.' Its shopping advice is specific: 'Read the label. Safe milk will have the word pasteurized on the label.' The CDC puts it plainly: 'While good practices on farms can reduce contamination, they cannot guarantee safety from harmful germs,' identifying Salmonella, E. coli and Listeria among the potential hazards of raw milk.

Why the trend matters now

The renewed spotlight comes as food-safety recalls keep raw dairy in the news — including recent recalls of raw milk cheese linked to illness — and as influencers promote unpasteurized products as more 'natural.' The agencies' position is that skipping the heating step adds risk without a demonstrated nutritional advantage. Readers should not treat social-media claims about raw milk as medical advice; anyone with questions about diet and infection risk should consult a clinician.

articles.title: FDA Floats Draft Peptide Compounding Policy Covering Six Peptides, Comments Open to November 13
articles.description: A draft enforcement-discretion policy published October 30 would let state-licensed pharmacies compound six peptides while the FDA develops its bulk substances list — but it approves no drug and is not binding.
articles.body:
The Department of Health and Human Services published a draft enforcement-discretion policy on October 30 covering compounding of certain peptide drug substances, with a notice of its availability in the Federal Register, according to a summary of the policy published October 31.

What the draft covers — and what it does not

Under the draft, HHS says it does not intend to take enforcement action against a state-licensed pharmacy, federal facility or licensed physician compounding a drug using one of six peptides in its Appendix A — BPC-157, Epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c and TB-500 as the acetate, and Semax as free base — under the conditions it sets, while the FDA's 503A bulks list is developed through rulemaking. It approves no drug: the notice states that compounded drugs are not FDA-approved. It does not cover 503B outsourcing facilities, nor products sold as 'research use only,' which FDA warning letters have called unapproved new drugs.

A draft, not a rule

The policy is a draft and is 'not binding on HHS or the public,' with comments open until November 13, 2026. HHS says it may revisit the policy if a safety signal or product-quality issue arises. Readers should not treat the draft as approval or as a safety endorsement of any peptide product; the distinction between a compounded drug made under enforcement discretion and an FDA-approved medicine remains the key point of the policy.

articles.title: Wise Wife Ground Cinnamon Recalled in 14 States Over Elevated Lead Levels
articles.description: SLR Food Distribution is recalling Wise Wife Brand Ground Cinnamon sold in 14 states after testing found elevated lead levels; no illnesses have been reported, according to the FDA announcement of October 29.
articles.sources: FDA via USA Today, People, Reader's Digest, October 29-31, 2026
articles.body:
A fall baking staple has been recalled in more than a dozen states for potential lead contamination, with the Food and Drug Administration announcing on October 29 that SLR Food Distribution Inc. is recalling its Wise Wife Brand Ground Cinnamon because it could contain elevated levels of lead.

Which product is affected

The recalled cinnamon comes in a 110-gram (3.88-ounce) clear plastic container with a black screw-top cap, carrying UPC 0688474302754 on the back label and a Best Before date of 4/25/2027. It was distributed to retail and grocery stores in Connecticut, Indiana, Kansas, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, North Carolina, Nebraska, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas, Virginia and Wisconsin between September 8, 2025, and June 28, 2026. The problem came to light after the Connecticut Agricultural Experiment Station tested a sample and found elevated lead levels; the Hicksville, New York-based company then voluntarily initiated the recall.

What consumers should do

No illnesses have been reported in connection with the recall, according to the FDA. Customers should not consume the recalled spice and should either discard it or return it to the place of purchase for a full refund, the agency said. Ground cinnamon has been under closer scrutiny since 2024, when the FDA issued a public health alert listing more than a dozen brands flagged for lead, and another cinnamon brand sold in six states was recalled for the same reason last month.

articles.title: FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to Voceryq, the First Plasmid DNA Immunotherapy in the US
articles.description: The FDA granted accelerated approval on October 30 to Voceryq, a treatment designed to reduce repeat surgery for adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis, a rare disease that causes growths in the airways.
articles.sources: FDA via EB News Daily, JBizNews, October 31, 2026
articles.body:
US regulators have granted accelerated approval to Voceryq, a new treatment intended to reduce repeat surgery for adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis, a rare disease that causes wart-like growths in the airways, the Food and Drug Administration announced on Friday, October 30.

A first for plasmid DNA immunotherapy

The FDA described Voceryq, made by Inovio Pharmaceuticals, as the first plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy approved in the United States. It targets human papillomavirus types 6 and 11, which cause the disease. It is not the first immunotherapy for the condition: the FDA approved Papzimeos, which uses a different technology, in August 2025. Surgery can remove the growths, but the virus can remain in tissue and patients may need procedures repeatedly over many years.

What the evidence shows — and what it does not

The decision drew on an open-label study involving 32 adults. Among 26 participants who had needed at least three surgeries in the preceding 12 months, seven — 27% — required no surgery during the first year after treatment. The approval does not establish a cure: it rests on reduced need for surgery, an intermediate outcome the FDA considers reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, and Inovio must conduct post-approval studies to verify that benefit. The company said it expects orders and shipments to begin in about 60 days, with full commercial deployment in the first quarter of 2027 — company forecasts, not confirmation the medicine is already available.

articles.title: FDA Approves At-Home Subcutaneous Induction for Skyrizi in Crohn's Disease
articles.description: The FDA has approved a subcutaneous induction regimen for Skyrizi in adults with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease, letting patients start treatment at home with an on-body injector.
articles.sources: AbbVie via Medical Update Online, October 31, 2026
articles.body:
AbbVie announced on October 31 that the US Food and Drug Administration has approved a subcutaneous induction regimen for Skyrizi (risankizumab-rzaa) for adults with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease.

Treatment that starts at home

Patients now have the option to start Skyrizi treatment at home, with induction doses delivered by an on-body injector induction pack, and then continue using an on-body injector once every eight weeks throughout maintenance treatment. The change removes the need for infusion-based induction for patients who choose the new regimen, a practical difference for a chronic condition that requires long-term therapy.

Backed by the AFFIRM trial

The approval is supported by positive results from the Phase 3 AFFIRM trial evaluating subcutaneous Skyrizi versus placebo in patients with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease. Skyrizi achieved superiority on the co-primary endpoints of clinical remission and endoscopic response at week 12. As with any prescription therapy, patients should discuss suitability, dosing and monitoring with their clinician rather than treating an approval announcement as a personal treatment recommendation.

articles.title: FDA Authorizes 24 Velo Nicotine Pouches, Bringing Total Authorized Pouches to 67
articles.description: The FDA authorized 24 new Velo Mini Pouch products on October 30, all containing 4 mg of nicotine, after finding they contain lower levels of harmful constituents than cigarettes and smokeless tobacco.
articles.body:
The US Food and Drug Administration authorized the marketing of 24 new nicotine pouch products on Friday, October 30, 2026, through the premarket tobacco product application pathway, the agency announced.

What was authorized

The authorized products are made by Modoral Brands Inc. under the Velo brand and all contain 4 mg of nicotine. They include three types of packaging for the Velo Mini Pouch and Velo Mini Pouch 2, each in four different flavors, reviewed under the agency's nicotine pouch pilot program, which enables a more streamlined review process.

Before any new tobacco product can be marketed legally in the US, it must undergo a rigorous scientific review in which the FDA considers the risks and benefits to the US population as a whole. The FDA's evaluation found that the newly authorized products contain lower levels of harmful and potentially harmful constituents compared to cigarettes and smokeless tobacco products, many of which were too low to be quantified, and no measurable levels of several carcinogenic constituents linked to increased oral cancer risk in smokeless tobacco users.

What it means — and does not mean

The agency said the authorizations underscore its commitment to providing greater access to products that can help adults aged 21 and older who smoke transition away from combusted cigarettes and smokeless tobacco products. Authorization is not an endorsement that the products are safe: nicotine pouches remain tobacco products, and the FDA's decision rests on a population-level assessment that they are appropriate for the protection of public health relative to the alternatives, not that they are risk-free.

To date, the FDA has authorized 67 nicotine pouches in total. The newly authorized products join that list, which the agency publishes on its authorized nicotine pouches page.

articles.title: FDA Updates Menopause Hormone Therapy Labels for Three More Products in Women's Health Push
articles.description: The FDA approved updated labeling for three additional menopausal hormone therapy products on October 30, removing outdated boxed-warning risk statements, as part of a wider effort to expand access to menopause care.
articles.body:
The US Department of Health and Human Services, through the Food and Drug Administration, on October 30, 2026 approved updated labeling for three additional menopausal hormone therapy products from two applicants, and provided an update on efforts to expand manufacturing capacity and availability of the therapies.

What changed

The three products with updated labeling are for estradiol transdermal patches. The action approves removal of the same outdated risk statements regarding cardiovascular disease, breast cancer and probable dementia from the boxed warning section that the FDA cleared for six products in February 2026. The agency said its actions are grounded in a sustained commitment to women's health as a cross-cutting priority.

The labeling effort supports President Trump's Executive Order, Advancing Women's Health to Improve Outcomes in All Phases of Life, signed on October 19, 2026. HHS said the First Lady was the impetus behind creating the executive order and the task force behind it.

Supply and access next

In November 2025, the FDA began engaging companies to submit proposed supplemental revisions to their hormone therapy labeling; to date, 29 drug companies have submitted proposed changes, and the FDA says it is working expeditiously with applicants on the remaining products. In addition to approving generic menopausal hormone therapies, the agency is working with sponsors to explore the potential for over-the-counter availability of vaginal estrogen products.

Patients and consumers have reported localized challenges with access, according to HHS, and the agency's parallel work on manufacturing changes aims to increase capacity and availability of the therapies for Americans who need them.

articles.title: FDA Declares Trader Joe's Chicken Wrap E. Coli Outbreak Over After 50 People Fell Ill
articles.description: The FDA has declared over the E. coli outbreak linked to chicken wraps sold at Trader Joe's, which sickened 50 people in August, while a separate new outbreak is under investigation.
articles.sources: Food Safety News, FDA outbreak update, October 28-29, 2026
articles.body:
The Food and Drug Administration has declared over the E. coli outbreak linked to multi-ingredient wraps with chicken, an outbreak that sickened 50 people during one week in August, according to an agency update on October 28.

Why the FDA says the case is closed

The implicated wraps were proactively removed from the market before the link to the outbreak was established, and the products people ate are past their shelf life and no longer available for purchase. The FDA said more detailed product information would not have provided consumers with an action they could take to prevent illness. Neither the FDA nor the USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service named the grocery chain in their outbreak reports, though the USDA confirmed to USA Today that the wraps came from Trader Joe's, and the company has said it pulled its Tarragon Chicken Salad Wraps from shelves in nine states.

What remains unresolved

The agencies have not publicly revealed the source of the E. coli contamination, what ingredients were traced, or which locations were inspected. The FDA said its outbreak investigation remains active even as the outbreak itself is declared over, and Food Safety News reports a separate new outbreak is now under investigation, with no details yet released.

A reminder on food safety

E. coli O157:H7 can cause severe stomach cramps, bloody diarrhea and, in serious cases, kidney failure, with young children and older adults at highest risk. Consumers who still have any suspect wraps in a freezer should discard them, and anyone with symptoms after eating a prepared chicken wrap should seek medical advice.

articles.title: FDA Recalls More Than 21,000 Bottles of Blood Pressure Drug Over Excess Active Ingredient
articles.description: More than 21,600 bottles of telmisartan and amlodipine tablets have been recalled after tests found some tablets may contain more telmisartan than specified.
articles.body:
More than 21,600 bottles of a blood pressure medication have been recalled in the United States after testing found some tablets may contain more of one active ingredient than the label specifies, according to FDA recall records.

Which product is affected

The recall covers telmisartan and amlodipine tablets, 40 mg/5 mg, supplied in 30-count bottles and manufactured for Mylan Pharmaceuticals by Viatris Inc. Five lots are affected: 3228113, 3228114 and 3228115, which expire October 31, 2026, and 3228120 and 3228121, which expire November 30, 2026. The recall was voluntarily initiated on October 1, 2026, and the FDA classified it as Class III, meaning adverse health consequences are considered unlikely.

What patients should do

Patients should check the lot number on their bottle and, if it matches, contact their dispensing pharmacist or prescribing clinician for product-specific guidance. Health experts advise against independently adjusting the dose or abruptly stopping prescribed blood pressure treatment, since sudden discontinuation carries its own risks. The recall does not cover every product containing telmisartan or amlodipine, so confirming the exact strength, bottle size and lot number is essential.

Why excess content matters

Even a Class III recall is a reminder that consistent dosing matters for blood pressure control: too much of an active ingredient can lower blood pressure further than intended, while switching products without guidance can disrupt treatment. Pharmacists can arrange a replacement supply, and patients with questions about symptoms should speak to their clinician promptly.

articles.title: FDA Recall: Miyoko's Plant-Based Butter Pulled in 10 States Over E. Coli, Yeast and Mold
articles.description: More than 1,300 cases of Miyoko's Creamery plant-based butter were recalled after lab reports flagged yeast, mold and E. coli contamination.
articles.sources: New York Post, Geo News, FDA enforcement report, October 28, 2026
articles.body:
A popular plant-based butter has been recalled in ten states after lab reports identified potential contamination with yeast, mold and E. coli, the US Food and Drug Administration said. Miyoko's Creamery European Style Salted Plant Milk Butter, made from cashew milk and plant oils by Prosperity Organic Foods Inc. of Boise, Idaho, was assigned a Class II risk level, meaning use of the product could cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences.

What to check in your fridge

The recall covers 1,304 cases, totalling 7,824 individual 8-ounce units, shipped in 6-pack cases with lot number 1007871 and a best-by date of November 5, 2026. The affected units were sold in Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Maryland, New Hampshire, New Jersey and Wisconsin. The recall began after supermarket chain Market Basket notified customers of high yeast levels that did not meet quality standards; the FDA classified the recall as Class II on October 23, following an initial recall on September 11, according to reports.

E. coli infections can cause severe stomach issues, diarrhoea, nausea and vomiting, and some strains risk hemolytic uremic syndrome, a life-threatening condition that can lead to kidney failure. Young children and older adults are particularly vulnerable to severe illness, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. As a Class II recall, the safest option is to toss the product or return it to the store.

articles.title: CDC: Drug-Resistant Germs Cause Nearly 9.7 Million US Infections a Year
articles.description: The CDC's 2026 Antimicrobial Resistance Threats Report estimates about 9.7 million drug-resistant infections and 50,800 deaths a year in the United States.
articles.sources: CDC 2026 Antimicrobial Resistance Threats Report, October 27, 2026
articles.body:
Drug-resistant germs cause an estimated 9.7 million infections and roughly 50,800 deaths a year in the United States, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's 2026 Antimicrobial Resistance Threats Report, released October 27. The estimates use 2023 data and new surveillance methods, and the agency warns that expanded data sources and methods make direct comparisons with earlier reports inappropriate.

The urgent threats

The CDC reclassified 19 pathogens into urgent, serious and concerning tiers, listing Candida auris, carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter, carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales and drug-resistant gonorrhea as urgent threats. The agency highlighted sharp rises in C. auris, up about tenfold since 2019, and the rapid spread of resistance genes such as NDM in CRE, while downgrading C. difficile to serious after falling rates.

Public health and medical groups say the findings raise the urgency for better infection control, broader genomic surveillance and financial incentives such as the PASTEUR Act to revive antibiotic and antifungal development. The report's message is blunt: resistance is no longer a future threat, it is already a leading, everyday killer, and slowing it will take stewardship in hospitals, farms and clinics alike.

articles.title: CDC Deputy Director Jennifer Shuford to Leave After Midterms, Report Says
articles.description: Jennifer Shuford, the CDC's deputy director and chief medical officer, will leave the Trump administration after next week's midterm elections, the Washington Post reported.
articles.body:
Jennifer Shuford, the deputy director of the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, will leave the Trump administration after next week's midterm elections, the Washington Post reported on Monday, citing sources. Shuford, a former Texas health commissioner, also serves as the CDC's chief medical officer and was hired in April as part of a team that included former deputy surgeon general Erica Schwartz, healthcare executive Sean Slovenski and FDA official Sara Brenner.

The reason for Shuford's departure was not immediately clear, the paper said, with one person attributing it to a family health issue and another saying she had disagreed with the administration's approach to vaccine policy. The CDC and the White House did not respond to requests for comment outside business hours, according to Reuters, which carried the report.

Departure follows vaccine policy shifts

The reported departure follows changes in the government's vaccine policy, with President Donald Trump unveiling plans to demand that vaccine makers split certain childhood shots into five separate doses. The step would advance a long-standing goal of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., whose promotion of a link between vaccines and autism has been repeatedly debunked by scientists, according to Reuters.

Shuford's exit, if confirmed, would add to turnover at the top of the nation's public health agencies during a period of significant policy change. The CDC plays a central role in disease surveillance, outbreak response and vaccine recommendations, and its leadership has faced intense scrutiny this year as the administration has moved to reshape health policy.

What is not yet confirmed

Because the report rests on unnamed sources, key details remain unconfirmed, including the exact timing of Shuford's departure and the reasons behind it. The Washington Post's account presents two different explanations, and neither the CDC nor the White House has publicly confirmed the move. Observers will be watching for an official announcement and for news of a successor, as the deputy director role carries significant responsibility for the agency's day-to-day operations.

The timing, just after the midterm elections, also places the departure in a politically charged moment. Health policy has featured prominently in the campaign, and any leadership change at the CDC is likely to draw attention from lawmakers and public health experts alike.

articles.title: FDA Clears Cullinan's Velinotamig Trial for Autoimmune Blood Disorders
articles.description: The FDA and Australia's regulator cleared Cullinan Therapeutics to start a global Phase 1b/2a trial of velinotamig in relapsing and refractory ITP and warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia.
articles.body:
Cullinan Therapeutics announced on Tuesday that the US Food and Drug Administration and Australia's Therapeutic Goods Administration have cleared the company to initiate a global Phase 1b/2a clinical trial of velinotamig in adults with relapsing and refractory immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) and warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (wAIHA). The open-label, multicenter study will evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, immunogenicity and preliminary clinical activity of the subcutaneously administered drug.

Velinotamig is a BCMAxCD3 T cell engager designed to deplete antibody-producing plasma cells. The study expands Cullinan's immunology portfolio into autoimmune cytopenias, evaluating a short-duration subcutaneous regimen in patients whose disease has not responded adequately to existing treatments.

Serious disorders with limited options

ITP and wAIHA are serious, potentially life-threatening autoimmune blood disorders in which pathogenic autoantibodies contribute to the destruction of platelets and red blood cells, respectively. Patients often experience significant disease burden, including debilitating fatigue and reduced quality of life, as well as severe manifestations such as bleeding in ITP and anemia in wAIHA.

Despite available therapies, many patients experience persistent or relapsing disease, remain dependent on chronic treatment, or develop substantial adverse events from current therapies. That gap is what Cullinan says its approach is designed to address, by targeting the plasma cells that produce the harmful antibodies rather than managing symptoms alone.

What the trial will test

The Phase 1b/2a study is designed to establish the safety and dosing of velinotamig while gathering early evidence of clinical activity. As an open-label trial, both researchers and participants will know who is receiving the drug, a standard design for early-stage studies focused on safety and dose-finding. Results from this stage will determine whether the drug advances to larger trials.

The dual clearance in the United States and Australia allows the company to run the trial across both countries, a common strategy for recruiting patients with rare conditions. For patients with relapsing and refractory disease, new trial options represent one of the few paths to treatments that go beyond currently approved therapies.

articles.title: Regeneron Extends US Ebola Supply Deal Worth About $270 Million Through 2031
articles.description: Regeneron extended its agreement with a US health authority to supply its Ebola treatment Inmazeb through 2031, as an outbreak in Africa spreads to four countries.
articles.body:
Regeneron said on Monday it extended its agreement with a U.S. health authority to provide additional supply of its Ebola treatment, amid a growing outbreak in Africa that has become the widest geographic spread of any Ebola outbreak on the continent to date.

The new agreement with the U.S. Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority, expanding a 2020 contract, will see Regeneron supply doses of its drug Inmazeb through 2031 for about $270 million. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Inmazeb in 2020 for the treatment of infection caused by Zaire ebolavirus.

An outbreak that keeps spreading

The current outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no approved specific antiviral treatment or licensed vaccine. Regeneron said it is testing its experimental therapy, maftivimab, as a potential treatment for the Bundibugyo virus.

The outbreak, first reported in the Democratic Republic of Congo in May, has now spread to four countries across East, Central and West Africa. The current outbreak has infected nearly 10,000 people and killed more than 4,800 in Congo, according to Reuters.

What Ebola does

Ebola is a severe viral illness that can cause fever, vomiting and diarrhea and, in severe cases, internal and external bleeding. Outbreaks spread through close contact with the bodily fluids of infected people, which is why isolation, protective equipment and safe burial practices are central to containment.

The scale of the current outbreak, combined with its spread across four countries, has raised concern among global health officials that containment will require sustained international effort, not just a local response.

Why the U.S. is stockpiling

The extended supply agreement is part of the U.S. government's preparedness strategy: keeping approved countermeasures on hand before a crisis reaches American shores. Inmazeb's approval for the Zaire strain makes it a cornerstone of that stockpile, even though the current outbreak involves a different strain.

That gap is exactly what Regeneron's experimental work targets. If maftivimab proves effective against Bundibugyo, it could fill one of the most dangerous holes in the world's Ebola defenses. For now, the drug remains investigational, and its testing is at an early stage.

Health officials stress that the immediate priority remains stopping transmission in the affected countries, through contact tracing, community engagement and care for patients. The supply deal, while significant, is a long-term insurance policy, not a substitute for the outbreak response now underway in Africa.

articles.title: FDA Warns San Francisco Fermented Foods Maker Over Pathogen Risks and Labeling
articles.description: The FDA has issued a warning letter to San Francisco manufacturer RDM Express over food safety and labeling violations involving its fermented cabbage products, kvas drink and pickles.
articles.body:
The Food and Drug Administration has issued a warning letter to a San Francisco food manufacturer after inspectors found deficiencies in its food safety plan, sanitation procedures and controls for refrigerated, ready-to-eat fermented cabbage products.

The letter names RDM Express Inc. of San Francisco. The agency also cited labeling violations involving the company's Russian-style kvas drink, sour cabbage and half-sour pickles, according to coverage of the letter by Food Safety News.

What inspectors found

Inspectors flagged problems in the company's food safety plan, its sanitation procedures and its controls for refrigerated, ready-to-eat fermented cabbage products. Refrigerated ready-to-eat foods are a particular focus for regulators because they are eaten without a cooking step that would kill pathogens, so the safety controls at the plant are the consumer's main protection.

The labeling violations cover the company's kvas drink, sour cabbage and half-sour pickles. Labels are not just marketing: for fermented and refrigerated products, accurate labeling tells consumers how to store a product safely and what is actually inside it.

How FDA warning letters work

As part of its enforcement activities, the FDA sends warning letters to entities under its jurisdiction. Business owners have 15 days to respond to a warning letter, laying out how they will correct the violations.

Warning letters are often not issued until companies have been given months or years to correct problems, and some letters are not posted for public view until weeks or months after they are sent. That means a warning letter usually represents the escalation of a long-running compliance conversation, not a first notice.

What it means for shoppers

A warning letter is not itself a recall, and the coverage of this letter does not report illnesses linked to the company's products. But it is a public signal that regulators found the company's safety systems wanting, and consumers who buy refrigerated fermented products should pay attention to storage instructions and expiration dates.

Shoppers who have concerns about a specific product can check the FDA's warning letter postings and the company's own communications for updates. The most important practical step is simple: keep refrigerated fermented foods refrigerated, follow the label, and discard anything that looks or smells off.

The case is a reminder that the fermented foods boom, from kimchi to kvas to craft pickles, sits squarely inside the food safety system. Small producers face the same rules as large ones, and the FDA's letter to RDM Express shows the agency is watching that fast-growing corner of the grocery aisle.

articles.title: Salmonella Oyster Recall Expands: What to Know About the Little Wicomico Outbreak
articles.description: The CDC reports 27 Salmonella Telelkebir illnesses in 12 states linked to Little Wicomico oysters, while the recalled oysters were distributed in 15 states plus DC. Do not eat them.
articles.sources: CDC, FDA, CIDRAP, ConsumerAffairs, Food Safety News
articles.body:
Federal health officials are warning consumers not to eat recalled oysters from Virginia's Little Wicomico Oyster Company, linked to a multistate Salmonella outbreak. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported on October 19, 2026, that 27 people in 12 states have been sickened with Salmonella Telelkebir infections, five have been hospitalized, and no deaths have been reported. Illnesses began between May 29 and September 14, 2026.

The company voluntarily recalled whole, in-shell oysters on October 9, 2026. The recall covers oysters harvested from September 18 through October 8, 2026, from the Little Wicomico River and Little Wicomico River Lower growing areas in Virginia. The company's certification number is VA-1421-SP. The Virginia Department of Health has also temporarily closed the Little Wicomico River harvest area as a precaution, and the company has stopped harvesting from the affected area and is cooperating with investigators.

Two different numbers — do not mix them up

Readers may see two different sets of figures, and they measure different things. The 27 illnesses in 12 states are the CDC's confirmed case count, with Pennsylvania reporting the most illnesses (eight), followed by New York (four) and Virginia (three). Separately, the recalled oysters were distributed to restaurants and retailers in 15 states and the District of Columbia: California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Maryland, Missouri, Nevada, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Texas, Virginia and Washington, D.C. Distribution is wider than the confirmed case count, and officials say the oysters may have been distributed further.

Food Safety News also reported that the Virginia Department of Health has documented 55 patients across 19 states — a higher tally than the CDC's 27 — reflecting differences in how state and federal counts are compiled and updated. The advice is the same regardless of which count you read: do not eat, sell or serve the recalled oysters.

How investigators linked the oysters

Of the 27 people counted by the CDC, 13 were interviewed, and 10 of them (77%) reported eating raw oysters, against a 1.6% background rate in CDC's FoodNet Population Survey. Traceback was possible for seven of the ten, and Little Wicomico River oysters were the only ones all seven had in common. Pennsylvania officials also sampled oysters at a distributor, and one sample harvested by the company from the Little Wicomico River was positive for Salmonella, with whole genome sequencing to determine whether it matches the outbreak strain still pending. Contaminated food can look, smell and taste normal, the FDA cautioned — so check tags and discard or return any affected oysters, and seek medical attention for severe symptoms.

articles.title: Graziers Raw Milk Cheese Recall: 13 Sick, 8 Hospitalized as FDA Issues Class I Warning
articles.description: Sierra Nevada Cheese Company recalled all Graziers raw milk cheeses after an E. coli O26:H11 outbreak sickened 13 people in 9 states, hospitalizing 8 and causing kidney complications in 3.
articles.sources: FDA, CDC via Times Now, Sierra Nevada Cheese Company recall notice, Mesa County Public Health
articles.body:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued its highest-risk warning for recalled Graziers raw milk cheese products after an E. coli outbreak sickened 13 people across nine states, hospitalized eight and left three with hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS), a serious complication that can cause kidney failure. No deaths have been reported. The FDA classified the recall as Class I on Monday, October 19, 2026 — meaning there is a reasonable probability that consuming or being exposed to the recalled products could cause serious health consequences or death.

The affected products are Sierra Nevada Graziers grass-fed raw milk cheeses, made by California-based Sierra Nevada Cheese Company of Willows, California. Varieties include medium cheddar, sharp cheddar, jalapeño jack and Monterey Jack, sold in 8-ounce and 16-ounce retail packages, 5-pound loaves for food service and wholesalers, and 40-pound cheddar blocks. The products were distributed in Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, Oregon, Texas, Washington and Wisconsin — 13 states of distribution, distinct from the nine states where illnesses were reported.

A recall with no lot code

Most recalls name a lot code and a date range. This one names neither. Sierra Nevada Cheese Company initiated the voluntary recall on September 28, 2026, after being contacted by the FDA regarding the ongoing FDA/CDC outbreak investigation, and the company said the investigation “has not been narrowed to a specific lot, date code, or production date,” so no batch could be cleared. The company immediately stopped production and shipment of all Graziers raw milk cheese, notified customers and issued notices through its website and social media.

According to information provided during the investigation, illnesses have been epidemiologically associated with consumption of Graziers Raw Milk Medium Cheddar, and the outbreak involves E. coli O26:H11, a strain of Shiga toxin-producing E. coli. The CDC reported 13 people infected as of September 25. Because some wholesale cheese may have been cut and repackaged, shoppers holding cheese without its original packaging have little to go on except the Graziers name — which is the practical reason the company chose a blanket recall.

What to do

Consumers who have purchased the recalled Graziers raw milk cheese products should not consume or serve them, and should return the product to the place of purchase for a refund or dispose of it. Check both refrigerators and freezers, because these cheeses may last a long time, and clean and sanitize any containers, shelves, knives, boards or surfaces that may have touched the product. Symptoms of E. coli infection usually begin 3 to 4 days after infection but can start any time between 1 and 14 days, and can include fever, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting and abdominal pain. Contact a doctor if you have concerns after eating a recalled product.

articles.title: CDC and FDA Performance Ratings Hit All-Time Lows in Gallup Poll
articles.description: Just 26% of Americans rate the CDC excellent or good and 25% say the same of the FDA — the lowest ratings Gallup has measured for either agency.
articles.sources: Gallup, Becker's Hospital Review, Fierce Healthcare
articles.body:
Performance ratings for the FDA and CDC have hit all-time lows, according to a Gallup poll reported on October 15, 2026. Gallup asked 1,000 U.S. adults to rate the job performance of 12 federal agencies and five Cabinet departments as excellent, good, only fair or poor. The poll was conducted September 1–17, 2026, by telephone, with a margin of error of plus or minus 4 percentage points.

Just 26% of Americans rated the CDC's performance as excellent or good, while a record-high 44% rated it poor. The FDA fared worse still: 25% rated it excellent or good, with 48% rating it poor. The FDA and CDC are the lowest-rated of the 12 agencies surveyed, and the only ones with higher poor ratings than excellent/good ratings. By contrast, the highest-rated agencies were the U.S. Postal Service at 58% and NASA at 53%.

A long fall from 2019

The CDC's decline has been steep. In 2019, 64% of Americans rated the CDC excellent or good. That share fell to 40% in 2021 and now stands at 26%, down five points from 2025 and 14 points from 2024. The FDA has historically been rated lower than the CDC, reaching only 46% in a 2017 survey; its current 25% is statistically similar to last year's 27%, but still the lowest Gallup has measured for the agency.

The partisan split tells much of the story — and it has flipped. Democrats' rating of the CDC dropped 14 points this year, to 20%, following a 31-point decline in 2025, while Republicans' ratings improved from 19% in 2024 to 32% this year. For the FDA, 36% of Republicans rated it excellent or good, up from 23% in 2024, compared with 18% of Democrats, down from 47% in 2024. Since 2019, Gallup notes, the party subgroup aligned with the incumbent president has always rated the FDA significantly more favorably.

Why it matters now

Gallup notes the agencies have been in the news recently — the CDC in connection with measles outbreaks amid attempts to change long-standing vaccine guidance, and the FDA in its coverage of a major cyclospora outbreak linked to lettuce that sickened people in many states. Congress will also need to weigh in again on funding for both agencies in the coming months. With a midterm election weeks away in which voters say health care costs will be a top issue, the poll is less a verdict on any single outbreak than a measure of how far public confidence in the country's health agencies has fallen — and how partisan that confidence has become.
